Populism: Political ideology emphasising the "common people"
A war correspondent in Afghanistan and Angola in the 1980s, this Oxford-educated Polish statesman later became his country's Foreign Minister and, since 2025, also Deputy Prime Minister — who is he?
Radosław Sikorski: Polish politician and journalist (born 1963)
This Congress politician led his party to victory in the 2023 election and became the second Chief Minister of Telangana — who is he?
Revanth Reddy: Chief Minister of Telangana (born 1969)
Raised in Russian-ruled Poland in a secular Jewish family, this Marxist theorist co-founded the anti-war Spartacus League and is remembered as a champion of socialist democracy — who is she?
A Harvard graduate and second cousin to a future U.S. president, this Boston revolutionary founded the Sons of Liberty and signed the Declaration of Independence — who was he?
Samuel Adams: Founding Father of the United States (1722–1803)
This Neo-Assyrian king destroyed Babylon in 689 BC and rebuilt Nineveh into a grand capital, but is most famous in the Hebrew Bible for his campaign in the Levant. Who was he?
Sennacherib: King of Assyria. Shortly after Sennacherib inherited the throne in 705 BC, Marduk-apla-iddina retook Babylon and allied with the Elamites.

During the Congo Crisis in 1961, a company of Irish UN peacekeepers was surrounded for five days by Katangese forces near a mining town before surrendering for lack of ammunition and water — which battle is this?
Siege of Jadotville: 1961 battle between Irish UN troops and Katanga during Congo Crisis.
Stepping out of his family's iron-and-steel business and into Parliament, this Conservative dominated British politics between the wars, serving as prime minister three separate times — who was he?
Stanley Baldwin: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom (1923–1924; 1924–1929; 1935–1937)

Fought from 1992 to 1997, this Central Asian conflict pitted rebels from the Garm and Gorno-Badakhshan regions, organized as the United Tajik Opposition, against a Russian-backed government — which conflict was it?
Tajikistani Civil War: Armed conflict in Tajikistan from 1992 to 1997.
Chief minister who engineered Henry VIII's break from Rome to annul his marriage to Catherine of Aragon, this powerful statesman was beheaded in 1540 — a loss the king later regretted. Who was he?
After leading Turkey's main miners' union and briefly working at the World Bank, this engineer-turned-statesman served as prime minister before becoming president from 1989 to 1993 — who is he?
Turgut Özal: President of Turkey from 1989 to 1993. ANAP won a parliamentary majority in the 1983 general election and Özal subsequently became the prime minister of Turkey.

Serving as Argentina's 38th vice president since 2023, this conservative politician founded a legal-studies center focused on terrorism victims and belongs to the La Libertad Avanza coalition — who is she?
Victoria Villarruel: Vice President of Argentina since 2023. Villarruel denies such accusations, maintaining that she does not support the "National Reorganization Process".
Sparked by a dispute over Maria Theresa's right to inherit the Habsburg throne, this 1740–1748 conflict began when Prussia seized the wealthy province of Silesia — what was this conflict called?
War of the Austrian Succession: 1740–1748 war between European powers.

Known as the 'Mother of the Nation,' this South African anti-apartheid activist and politician served in parliament and led the ANC Women's League after marrying the country's future president in 1958 — who is she?
Winnie Mandela: South African activist and politician (1936–2018)

After helping secure the Qing dynasty's abdication, this Chinese general became the Republic's first formal president, only to declare himself emperor in 1915 and abdicate again months later — who was he?
Yuan Shikai: First president of the Republic of China (1859–1916)
Which one below was born first?
Qian Xuesen (born 1911) is the earliest of the four. Qian received his undergraduate education in mechanical engineering at National Chiao Tung University in Shanghai in 1934.
Who among these was born first?
Ma Jun (mechanical engineer) (born 200) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four was born earliest?
Henry Vaughan (born 1621) is the earliest of the four. Henry Vaughan (1621 – 23 April 1695) was a Welsh metaphysical poet, author and translator writing in English, and a medical physician.
Which of these four dates back furthest?
Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is an astronomer?
Bruno Rossi is an astronomer. Bruno Benedetto Rossi ( ROSS-ee, Italian: [ˈbruːno beneˈdetto ˈrossi]; 13 April 1905 – 21 November 1993) was an Italian-American experimental physicist.
Which of these four is a mathematician?
Hilary Putnam is a mathematician. Outside philosophy, Putnam contributed to mathematics and computer science.
What is the atomic number of Indium?
Indium: It is a silvery-white post-transition metal and one of the softest elements.
What is the atomic number of Scandium?
Scandium is a chemical element; it has symbol Sc and atomic number 21.
In what year was Stephen Hawking born?
Stephen Hawking: Hawking was born in Oxford into a family of physicians.
In what year was Richard Sackler born?
Richard Sackler: Sackler and Purdue's role in the epidemic led to many lawsuits and fines, with the company filing bankruptcy in 2019.
In what year was Aristotle born?
Aristotle (Ancient Greek: Ἀριστοτέλης, romanized: Aristotélēs; 384–322 BC) was an ancient Greek philosopher and polymath.
In what year did Abraham Maslow die?
Abraham Maslow: Maslow was a psychology professor at Cornell University, Brooklyn College, Brandeis University, The New School for Social Research, and Columbia University.
In what year did Kevin Mitnick die?
Kevin Mitnick: Kevin David Mitnick (August 6, 1963 – July 16, 2023) was an American computer security consultant, author, and convicted hacker.
In what year was Mass–energy equivalence discovered?
Mass–energy equivalence: In physics, mass–energy equivalence is the relationship between mass and energy in a system's rest frame.
Which company manufactures Harrier jump jet?
Harrier jump jet: Hawker Siddeley. The Harrier emerged as the only truly successful V/STOL design of the many attempted during that era.
NHIndustries NH90: Airbus Helicopters. The NHIndustries NH90 is a medium-sized European twin-engine multi-role military helicopter.
Which country is Hawker Hunter from?
Hawker Hunter: United Kingdom. The all-weather/night fighter role was filled by the Gloster Javelin.
Who is credited with discovering Bohrium?
Bohrium: Yuri Oganessian. Bohrium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Bh and atomic number 107.
Who is credited with discovering 10 Hygiea?
10 Hygiea: Annibale de Gasparis. 10 Hygiea is a large asteroid in the outer region of the main asteroid belt, between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.
Who is credited with discovering Nickel?
Nickel: Axel Fredrik Cronstedt. Nickel is a chemical element; it has symbol Ni and atomic number 28.
Home to both edible and poisonous species, this fungal genus supplies the West's most popular cultivated mushrooms, including the everyday button mushroom — which genus is it?
Agaricus is a genus of mushroom-forming fungi containing both edible and poisonous species, with over 400 members worldwide and possibly again as many disputed or newly discovered species.

This central nervous system stimulant treats ADHD and narcolepsy today, but was once prescribed for nasal congestion and depression, and remains tightly controlled due to its abuse potential — name the drug?

Amphetamine is a central nervous system (CNS) stimulant that is used in the treatment of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and narcolepsy; it is also used to treat binge eating disorder in the form of lisdexamfetamine.
Its Latin name means 'water-carrier,' and this zodiac constellation sits between Capricornus and Pisces, in a region of the sky nicknamed 'the Sea' for its watery neighbors — which constellation?

Aquarius (constellation) is an equatorial constellation of the zodiac, between Capricornus and Pisces. Its name is Latin for "water-carrier" or "cup-carrier", and its traditional astrological symbol is (♒︎), a representation of water.
Technically a giant member of the grass family, this plant's tallest species can grow stalks over 150 feet long and weigh up to 450 kilograms — what plant is it?
Bamboo are a diverse group of mostly evergreen perennial flowering plants making up the subfamily Bambusoideae of the grass family Poaceae.

A thin-leaved deciduous hardwood related to alders and hazels, this genus of trees is widespread across the Northern Hemisphere's temperate and boreal climates, typically as a short-lived pioneer species — name the tree?
Birch is a thin-leaved deciduous hardwood tree of the genus Betula, in the family Betulaceae, which also includes alders, hazels, and hornbeams.

He won a share of the 1973 Nobel Prize in Physics for an effect he discovered in 1962 while still a Cambridge Ph.D. student — then later turned, controversially, to Transcendental Meditation. Which physicist is he?
Brian Josephson (born 4 January 1940) is a British theoretical physicist and emeritus professor at the University of Cambridge.

This sweet, aromatic orange-fleshed melon goes by different names depending on where you are — 'rockmelon' in Australia and New Zealand, 'spanspek' in Southern Africa — and can weigh up to 5 kilograms. What fruit is this?
Cantaloupe (also spelled cantaloup and cantelope;, or) is a type of true melon (Cucumis melo) with sweet, aromatic, and usually orange flesh.
Sometimes called melde or wild spinach, this weedy annual plant is often distinguished from its relatives in the same genus as the 'white' goosefoot — which plant?
Chenopodium album is a fast-growing annual plant in the flowering plant family Amaranthaceae.
The smallest member of the cockatoo family, this Australian parrot is recognized for its expressive crest and long tail feathers, and is a hugely popular pet bird. What bird is it?

Cockatiel (Nymphicus hollandicus), also known as the weero/weiro or quarrion, is a species of small- to medium-sized parrot belonging to the cockatoo family (Cacatuidae), of which it is the smallest member.
This trailing evergreen vine produces a tart berry that starts light green and turns bright red as it ripens on low, creeping stems. What fruit is it?
Cranberry are a group of evergreen dwarf shrubs or trailing vines in the subgenus Oxycoccus of the genus Vaccinium.

This condition's four subtypes include one caused by kidneys that don't respond to a hormone called vasopressin and another linked to excessive fluid intake from a damaged thirst mechanism — what is it?
Diabetes insipidus (DI) is a condition characterized by large amounts of dilute urine and increased thirst.
This social science examines the production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services, analyzing everything from individual agents to entire economies. What discipline is this?
Economics is a social science that studies the production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services.
This American physicist won a Nobel Prize for inventing a particle accelerator and later worked on uranium-isotope separation for the Manhattan Project. Who is he?
Ernest Lawrence (August 8, 1901 - August 27, 1958) was an American physicist who received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1939 for his invention of the cyclotron.
With over two hundred species across fifty genera, this bird family includes canaries, siskins, redpolls, grosbeaks, and the Hawaiian honeycreepers — which family of seed-eating passerines?
Finch are small to medium-sized passerine birds in the family Fringillidae.
Found on every continent except Antarctica, this lizard lacks eyelids — instead its eyeballs are covered by a transparent membrane called a brille. What is it?
Gecko are small, mostly carnivorous lizards that have a wide distribution, found on every continent except Antarctica.
Bred for centuries to hunt by sight and speed rather than scent, this ancient dog breed's deep chest, flexible spine, and long legs make it one of the fastest breeds alive. Name the breed?
Greyhound is a breed of dog and a sighthound. It is an ancient breed historically developed for hunting game by sight and speed, and has later been used in organised coursing and greyhound racing.

This field of study concerns the methodological principles of interpretation — especially of biblical, philosophical, and wisdom texts — and has been broadly applied across law, history, and theology — what's it called?

Hermeneutics is the study of the methodological principles of interpretation, especially the interpretation of biblical texts, wisdom literature, and philosophical texts. As necessary, hermeneutics may include the art of understanding and communication.
Related to the sodium and calcium compounds found in household bleach, this chlorine-based oxidizer also occurs naturally as part of the human immune system. What is it?
Hypochlorous acid is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula ClOH, also written as HClO, HOCl, or ClHO.
Eaten raw or turned into jams and wine, this round Brazilian fruit is famous for growing directly on the trunk of its own tree — what is it?
Jabuticaba is a round, edible fruit produced by a jaboticaba tree (Plinia cauliflora), also known as Brazilian grapetree.

An Alberta-raised classical liberal who earned his PhD in clinical psychology at McGill and taught at Harvard before the University of Toronto, this commentator drew huge attention in the late 2010s — who is he?
Jordan Peterson (born 12 June 1962) is a Canadian psychologist, author, and media commentator.

Born of Peranakan Chinese cuisine and beloved in Singapore and Malaysia, this spicy noodle dish swims in a rich coconut-curry soup soured with tamarind, topped with prawns or chicken — what's its name?
Laksa is a spicy noodle dish popular in Southeast Asia.
This ACE inhibitor can take up to four weeks for full effect and is also used to prevent kidney problems in people with diabetes — which medication?
Lisinopril is a medication belonging to the drug class of angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors and is used to treat hypertension (high blood pressure), heart failure, and heart attacks.
Recognizable by the male's iridescent green head, this widespread dabbling duck species has been introduced to countries from New Zealand to South Africa far beyond its native range — what is it?
Mallard (Anas platyrhynchos) is a dabbling duck that breeds throughout the temperate and subtropical Americas, Eurasia, and North Africa.

This mammal family, uniting skunks and stink badgers, is defined by highly developed scent glands used to ward off predators, and was only split from the weasel family in the 1990s — what family is it?
Mephitidae is a family of mammals comprising the skunks and stink badgers.
In 1812 Étienne Geoffroy grouped the apes with the Cercopithecidae under the name Catarrhini, or "Old World" members of this familiar simian group — what common name is it?
Monkey is a common name that may refer to most mammals of the infraorder Simiiformes, also known as simians.
This silvery lanthanide, found in the minerals monazite and bastnäsite, is about as common as cobalt or nickel despite its 'rare earth' label — which element?
Neodymium is a chemical element; it has symbol Nd and atomic number 60.
Founder of the charity Volnoe Delo and the industrial group Basic Element, which Russian oligarch led both En+ Group and Rusal until stepping down in 2018?
Oleg Deripaska (born 2 January 1968) is a Russian oligarch and billionaire.
Believed to have originated in Sardinia and cultivated since around the 3rd century BC, this flowering herb native to Greece and North Africa is a kitchen staple worldwide — what is it?
Parsley (Petroselinum crispum), is a species of flowering plant in the family Apiaceae that is native to Greece, the Balkans, Algeria and Morocco.
Colorless in acid and a vivid pink in base, which phthalein dye is the chemist's go-to indicator for acid-base titrations?
Phenolphthalein (feh-NOL(F)-th-leen) is a chemical compound with the formula C20H14O4 and is often written as "HIn", "HPh", "phph" or simply "Ph" in shorthand notation.

This academic field studies systems of governance and power, favoring descriptive and empirical analysis of behavior and institutions over the value judgments used in philosophy about the state — name the discipline?
Political science (sometimes abbreviated as poli sci) is a field which aims to study the scientific aspect of politics.

Named early in the history of microbiology for its widespread presence in water and plant seeds, which genus of gram-negative bacteria includes an opportunistic human pathogen infamous in hospitals as well as plant and soil-dwelling species?
Pseudomonas is a genus of gram-negative bacteria belonging to the family Pseudomonadaceae in the class Gammaproteobacteria.
Named from the Latin word for 'net', this light-sensitive layer lining the back of the eye functions much like the film or sensor inside a camera. Name this part of the eye?

This zodiac constellation, whose Latin name means 'archer,' is traditionally depicted as a centaur drawing a bow, and its territory in the southern sky contains the center of the Milky Way galaxy. What constellation is this?
Sagittarius (constellation) is one of the constellations of the zodiac and is located in the Southern celestial hemisphere.

Triggered by certain serotonergic medications, this group of symptoms can range from mild high blood pressure to severe, potentially fatal spikes in body temperature and dangerous muscle breakdown — what's it called?
Serotonin syndrome (SS) consists of a group of symptoms that may occur with the use of certain serotonergic medications or drugs.
Known in Hispanic America as guanábana and easily killed by a touch of frost, which Annona fruit blends flavors of strawberry, apple, and sour citrus?
Soursop (also called graviola, guyabano, and in Hispanic America guanbana) is the fruit of Annona muricata, a broadleaf, flowering, evergreen tree.
The only surviving tiger population in the Sunda Islands, found on the Indonesian island of Sumatra after its Bali and Javan cousins went extinct in the 20th century — what is it?
Sumatran tiger is a population of Panthera tigris sondaica on the Indonesian island of Sumatra.
This vast domain of human practice — divided into visual, literary, and performing branches — lets people transmit values, ideas, and experiences across generations. What is it?
The arts are a vast range of human practices involving creative expression, storytelling, and cultural participation.

This invasive annual plant, native to warm regions of Eurasia and Africa but now found in North America and Australia, produces small woody burrs with sharp spines capable of piercing bare feet. What plant is this?
Tribulus terrestris is an annual plant in the caltrop family (Zygophyllaceae) widely distributed around the world.
Its Latin name means 'maiden,' and it's the largest zodiac grouping in the sky, home to the bright star Spica between Leo and Libra — which one?
Virgo (constellation) is one of the constellations of the zodiac. The ecliptic intersects the celestial equator within this constellation and Pisces.

This Greek economist served as Finance Minister under PM Alexis Tsipras during the 2015 debt crisis, becoming internationally known for opposing EU-imposed austerity, before co-founding the left-wing party DiEM25 — who is he?
Yanis Varoufakis (born 24 March 1961) is a Greek economist, academic, author, and politician.

Nicknamed wolfsbane, monkshood, and devil's helmet, this highly toxic genus of over 250 mountain-dwelling flowering plants thrives in moist, well-draining soils across the Northern Hemisphere — what is it?
Aconitum: Genus of flowering plants in the buttercup family Ranunculaceae.
Which Swiss chemist was the first person to synthesize and personally experience the effects of LSD, later isolating the active compounds in magic mushrooms?
Named for its males' mating call, which sounds like a farm animal bellowing, this large amphibian native to eastern North America has been introduced worldwide as a food source — which species?
American bullfrog: Species of amphibian. It typically inhabits large permanent water bodies such as swamps, ponds, and lakes.
Evolved from vespoid wasp ancestors in the Cretaceous, these insects are easily spotted by their elbowed antennae and slender, node-waisted bodies — what are they?
Ant: Family of insects. Nearly all ant colonies also have some fertile males called "drones" and one or more fertile females called "queens" (gynes).
Caused by excessive exposure to silver dust or compounds, this condition turns the skin a striking blue or blue-gray shade, especially in sun-exposed areas — what's it called?
Argyria: Medical condition. The most dramatic symptom of argyria is that the skin turns blue or blue-gray, and is usually most prominent in sun-exposed areas of the skin.
Native to tropical Southeast Asia, this small tree bears bell-shaped rose-to-purple flowers and a ridged fruit that forms star-shaped slices when cut crosswise — which species?
Averrhoa carambola: Species of tree. It is a small tree or shrub that grows 5 to 12 m (16 to 39 ft) tall, with rose to red-purple flowers.

Nicknamed 'Huey,' this American utility helicopter became the first turbine-powered rotorcraft in U.S. military service, developed in the 1950s to meet an Army need for medical evacuation and utility missions. Which aircraft?
Bell UH-1 Iroquois: Huey family of American military utility helicopters.
This insect order unites cockroaches with termites, after genetic evidence showed termites are actually evolved, eusocial cockroaches. What's the order called?
Blattodea: Order of insects that includes cockroaches and termites.
Created in 1993 by Swiss student Urban Müller, this esoteric programming language uses just eight simple commands and is often cited as a 'Turing tarpit' — what is it called?
Brainfuck: Esoteric, minimalist programming language. While Brainfuck is fully Turing-complete, it is not intended for practical use but to challenge and amuse programmers.
Discovered in 1817 simultaneously by two German chemists as an impurity in zinc carbonate, this soft silvery-white metal shares chemical traits with zinc and mercury — which element?
Cadmium: Chemical element with atomic number 48 (Cd)
Called the 'father of modern taxonomy,' which Swedish biologist formalized the two-name system for naming living things and was later ennobled as von Linné?
Carl Linnaeus: Swedish biologist and physician (1707–1778)
First flown in 1955 as a tricycle-gear evolution of an earlier taildragger model, this four-seat high-wing aircraft is the most-produced plane in history — which model is it?
Cessna 172: Propeller driven single engine aircraft.

Most often documented in boxers and football players, this neurodegenerative disease is linked to repeated blows to the head and can worsen into dementia — what's its name, usually shortened to three letters?
Chronic traumatic encephalopathy: Neurodegenerative disease caused by head injury.
Thought extinct since the age of dinosaurs 66 million years ago, this lobe-finned fish was found alive off the west Indian Ocean, more closely related to lungfish than typical fish — what is it?
This transparent structure at the front of the eye provides about two-thirds of its focusing power and can be reshaped with LASIK surgery — what is it?
Cornea: Transparent front layer of the eye. The cornea is the transparent front part of the eye which covers the iris, pupil, and anterior chamber.
Native to South and Southeast Asia and often sold as fresh stems, this tropical plant known as West Indian lemon grass can't survive a frost — what is it?
A fluorinated glucocorticoid, this medication treats everything from severe allergies and asthma to brain swelling and croup, and is given to ease preterm-labor outcomes — what is it?
Dexamethasone: Corticosteroid medication. The effects of dexamethasone are frequently seen within a day and last for about three days.
Also called Trisomy 21, this condition is caused by an extra copy of a single chromosome and grows more likely with a mother's age — from under 0.1% at 20 to about 3% at 45. What is it?
This unit of energy equals the kinetic energy a single electron gains while crossing an electric potential difference of one volt — what is it called?
Sometimes abbreviated ETM, this antibiotic treats everything from respiratory infections to syphilis and is the eye ointment routinely dabbed on newborns to prevent eye infections. What is it?
Erythromycin: Antibiotic medication. Erythromycin (sometimes abbreviated ETM in reports) is an antibiotic used for the treatment of a number of bacterial infections.
Native to the Iberian Peninsula and introduced to hundreds of locations worldwide, this grassland herbivore digs extensive burrow networks called warrens — what is it?

This branch of Islamic scholarship interprets the Quran and sunnah through jurist reasoning, producing fatwas — while sharia itself is seen as unchanging, this human field is considered fallible. What is it called?
Fiqh: Islamic jurisprudence. Thus, whereas sharia is considered immutable and infallible by Muslims, fiqh is considered fallible and changeable.

Making up roughly 88% of all living amphibians, this short-bodied, tailless order gets its name from Ancient Greek for 'without tail' — and its warty-skinned members are casually dubbed toads. What is it?
Frog: Order of amphibians. The eggs then hatch into fully aquatic larvae called tadpoles, which have tails and internal gills.
Also known as cranesbills for their pointed seed pods, this 422-species genus bears five-petaled, often veined flowers and includes at least one protocarnivorous species — what's the genus?
This system of rules governing clauses, phrases, and word use is often absorbed unconsciously in childhood, long before anyone studies its syntax formally — what field?
Grammar: Structural rules of a language.

Marketed under a well-known brand name, this typical antipsychotic treats everything from schizophrenia to Tourette tics, but carries risks of tardive dyskinesia and dangerous QT-interval prolongation — what drug is it?
Haloperidol: Typical antipsychotic medication. Haloperidol, sold under the brand name Haldol among others, is a typical antipsychotic medication.
Some called egrets and others bitterns, these 75 species of long-legged, long-beaked wading birds make up the family Ardeidae — what are they?
Heron: Family of birds. The OED also observes that shiterow or shederow are terms used for herons, and also applied as derogatory terms meaning a thin, weakly person.
A colorless, flammable liquid with an ammonia-like odor, this N2H4 compound foams polymer plastics, fills airbag gas generators, and serves as a storable spacecraft propellant. What is it?
Hydrazine: Colorless flammable liquid with an ammonia-like odor. It is a simple pnictogen hydride, and is a colourless flammable liquid with an ammonia-like odour.
The world's largest jet airliner when it first flew in 1963, this Soviet quad-engine jetliner entered Aeroflot service with a Moscow-to-Montreal flight in 1967. What aircraft?
Ilyushin Il-62: Soviet long-range narrow-body four-engined jet airliner.
An Indian polymath and pioneer of radio microwave optics, he's also considered the father of Bengali science fiction — and even has a crater on the Moon named for him. Who was he?
Jagadish Chandra Bose: Physicist, biologist and botanist (1857–1937)
On January 26, 1926, this Scottish inventor gave the world's first demonstration of a working mechanical television system — who is he?
Derived from Greek words for 'movement' and 'study,' this scientific field examines biomechanics, motor control, and rehabilitation to understand how the human body moves — what field is this?
Kinesiology: Study of human body movement. Kinesiology addresses physiological, anatomical, biomechanical, pathological, neuropsychological principles and mechanisms of movement.

The smallest member of the genus Mustela, this slender carnivore has been introduced to New Zealand, Malta, Crete, the Azores, and São Tomé despite being native across Eurasia and North Africa — what is it?
Element number 3, this soft silvery-white alkali metal is the least dense metal of all and so reactive it must be stored under oil or in an inert atmosphere — what is it?
Lithium: Chemical element with atomic number 3 (Li)
Found in the hundreds inside most animal cells but almost never in plant cells, this acidic, enzyme-packed organelle serves as the cell's degradation center — which organelle?
Lysosome: Cell membrane organelle. A lysosome (/ˈlaɪsəˌsoʊm/) is a membrane-bound organelle that is found in all animal cells (except red blood cells), and rarely in plant cells.
The first Mexican-born scientist to win the Nobel Prize in Chemistry, this physical chemist shared the 1995 award for revealing how CFC gases threaten the ozone layer — who?
This mammal family — skunks and stink badgers — was reclassified out of the weasel family in the 1990s after genetic evidence, and turns out to be closest kin to red pandas and raccoons. What is it?
Mephitidae: Family of mammals. In taxonomic order, the living species of Mephitidae are:.
Known to NATO as 'Halo,' this Soviet-designed aircraft holds the record as the largest helicopter ever built in serial production — which one?
Mil Mi-26: Soviet/Russian heavy transport helicopter.

This Japanese biologist used diffusion equations to calculate how likely a gene is to take over a population, and in 1968 proposed the "neutral theory" that genetic drift, not just selection, drives molecular evolution — who was he?
First identified from an 1856 fossil in a German valley, this group of archaic humans roamed Europe and Asia until vanishing around 40,000 years ago as modern humans arrived — who were they?

As the United States' first swept-wing fighter jet, this Korean War-era aircraft dueled Soviet MiG-15s in some of history's earliest jet-to-jet battles — which plane, produced in more than 7,800 units?
North American F-86 Sabre: Family of US fighter aircraft.

The world's most widespread and commercially important cactus species, this domesticated crop is grown both as a fruit and for its edible vegetable pads, likely originating in central Mexico — which species?
Opuntia ficus-indica: Species of cactus. It is grown primarily as a fruit crop, and also for the vegetable nopales and other uses.
One researcher catalogued as many as 549 varieties of this psychological category, defined by intense arousal toward things that aren't sexual by nature — what is the term?
This order of hoofed mammals — horses, rhinos, and tapirs — bears its weight on an odd number of toes and digests plant fiber in its intestines rather than a multi-chambered stomach. Which order?
Perissodactyla: Order of hoofed mammals. Perissodactyla (from Ancient Greek περισσός, perissós 'odd' and δάκτυλος, dáktylos 'finger, toe'), or odd-toed ungulates, is an order of ungulates.

This French polymath's five-volume 'Celestial Mechanics' recast Newtonian physics in the language of calculus, and he pioneered both a widely used integral transform and helped shape Bayesian probability — who is he?
This plant genus — whose members go by names like poplar, aspen, and cottonwood — includes the first tree species ever to have its complete genome sequenced, in 2006 — what genus is it?
Populus: Genus of plants. Populus is a genus of 25–30 species of deciduous flowering plants in the family Salicaceae, native to most of the Northern Hemisphere.
Flagged by the WHO as one of the greatest antibiotic-resistance threats to humans, this rod-shaped bacterium causes hospital infections like ventilator-associated pneumonia — which pathogen?
Pseudomonas aeruginosa: Species of bacterium. P. aeruginosa is able to selectively inhibit various antibiotics from penetrating its outer membrane and has high resistance to several antibiotics.
Named for the ragged look of its leaves, this genus of flowering plants causes up to half of all pollen-related allergy cases despite a genus name meaning 'food of the gods' — which plant?
Ragweed: Genus of plants. The name "ragweed" is derived from "ragged" + "weed," coming from the ragged appearance of the plant's leaves.
Also called vitamin B2, this nutrient forms two key coenzymes for energy metabolism, can be prescribed for corneal thinning, and taken orally may cut down migraines in adults — which vitamin is it?
Riboflavin: Vitamin, dietary supplement, and yellow food dye.

Nicknamed 'The Kite' (or perhaps 'The Dragon'), this Swedish supersonic fighter-interceptor's innovative double-delta wing traces back to 1948 and entered frontline service in March 1960 — which aircraft?
Saab 35 Draken: 1955 Swedish fighter aircraft. The full-scale production version entered service with frontline squadrons of the Swedish Air Force on 8 March 1960.

Named after a colourful terrestrial flower, this predatory marine cnidarian is typically a single polyp anchored to a hard surface — a tentacled relative of coral and jellyfish, but with no medusa stage. What is it?
Sea anemone: Marine animals of the order Actiniaria.
